newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil senator proposes changes in Vale sale model.
newsitem.headline: Brazil senator proposes changes in Vale sale model.

text.p: Brazil could change the model for privatization of mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce by offering more shares to the public, senator Antonio Carlos Magalhaes said on Monday.

"I think we could make the public participate more in Vale's privatization by adopting an English privatization model," Magalhaes told reporters after a luncheon at the Sao Paulo Stock Exchange (Bovespa).

Under Vale's sale plan, an initial sale of a 40-45 percent block of voting shares in the company would begin in February. The remainder would be offered to employees and to domestic and foreign investors in a second and third phases.
Magalhaes, a powerful senator from the Liberal Front Party (PFL), said Vale's privatization schedule could be modified "once new proposals (for the Vale selloff) emerge."
The senator said he would present soon President Fernando Henrique Cardoso the proposal to allow more public participation in the company's sale.
Magalhaes also said Vale's privatization has nothing to do with discussions over the re-election amendment.

He side-stepped questions about criticism from former presidents Itamar Franco and Jose Sarney who were reported to have suggested he might trade his opposition to re-election for more Senate oversight of the Vale sale.
Regarding the re-election, Magalhaes said he would try to convince Sao Paulo mayor and PPB leader Paulo Maluf to back the proposal.
"I want to tell him of the advantages of having someone with his prestige behind the re-election," he said, before heading for a meeting with Maluf.
Opposition to the re-election amendment, which would give Cardoso the chance for a second term, has been led by Maluf, who himself wants to run for president in the next elections.
